17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans ~ 2323 West Grand Avenue, Chicago, IL

Proposed Zoning:  _B2-5 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Lot Area: Approximately 14,910 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to redevelop the subject property with a new
five-story mixed-use building containing 2,700 sq. ft. of commercial/retail
space and an attached off-street parking garage on the first floor. The
proposed building will contain fifty-two (52) dwelling units above and will
feature a roof top deck. The proposed building will measure approximately
57 ft.-2 in. in height. The subject property is a Transit Served Location and
will be supported twenty-six (26) off-street parking spaces within the
attached garage. The subject lot is a through lot with two (2) street frontages
(West Grand Avenue to the north and West Ferdinand Street to the south).
Pursuant to Sec, 17-13-0303-D optional Administrative Adjustment and
Variation and pursuant to Secs. 17-13-1003-EE, 17-13-1003-P, Q, R, and
X, and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the Applicant is
seeking to decrease the residential off-street parking ratio from 100% (52
parking spaces) to 50% (26 parking spaces), to not comply with the TSL
design guidelines on the lot’s West Ferdinand Street frontage, to reduce the
ground floor commercial space floor area to 2,700, reduce the front setback
on the subject lot’s West Ferdinand Street frontage for floors containing
residential units from 30 feet to 2 ft., and is seeking all zoning relief
necessary, as needed and as allowed by the Chicago Zoning Code, for the
attached plans.

(A) The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 62,100 square feet (4.16 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 286.73 square feet per D.U.
(52 residential units)

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1, The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 391 linear feet of the Western Avenue CTA bus
line corridor. The proposed mixed-use building containing one (1) commercial space and
attached parking garage at grade and fifty-two (52) residential units above will be
supported by twenty-six (26) off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-
EE, the Applicant is seeking to permit a reduction in the residential off-street parking ratio
from 100% (52 parking spaces) to 50% (26 parking spaces).

2. The Applicant is seeking relief from the requirements of Sec. 17-4-0504 for the location of
the mixed-use building on the subject lot. The subject lot is a through lot with frontage on
both West Grand Avenue and West Ferdinand Street. The proposed location of the main
building door and entryway will be on the lot’s West Grand Avenue frontage and will have
a front setback of 12 inches. The building’s first floor was designed with windows facing
the sidewalk located along West Grand Avenue. The proposed building will have a front
setback of 2 ft. from the lot’s West Ferdinand Street frontage.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Western Avenue bus line corridor. The Applicant believes the
redevelopment of an underutilized lot will improve the subject area for residents and other
commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain approximately 2,700 sq. ft. of commercial
space and an attached parking garage at grade and fifty-two (52) residential units above.
The proposed building will be supported by twenty-six (26) off-street parking spaces. The
Applicant is seeking administrative approval to permit the off-street parking reduction for
the residential units pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace an underutilized
lot with a new mixed-use building, which will provide additional residential housing
thereby meeting market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to a designated
CTA bus line corridor (Bus Routes 49 and 49x), the Applicant believes the project provides
transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management
Plan rules promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an area in need.
